newsitem.title: VIETNAM: "Social evils" to be purged in Ho Chi Minh City.
newsitem.headline: "Social evils" to be purged in Ho Chi Minh City.

text.p: A new clampdown on drug abuse, prostitution and other "social evils" has been launched in Ho Chi Minh City, the daily Vietnam News said on Tuesday.
Officials in the country's southern metropolis declined to confirm the state-controlled newspaper's report, which said the purge was decided after a two-day review by the Interior Ministry.
"The campaign will include checking the management and activities at discotheques, dancing clubs and restaurants in 22 districts for drug abuse, prostitution and noise pollution," the paper said.
Checks would also be carried out at the city's hotels, restaurants, massage houses and hairdressing salons -- which sometimes double as sex parlours.

However, it was not clear when the new drive had started or whether it would match the severity of last year's onslaught on social evils, when sex videos and magazines were destroyed in public and hundreds of prostitutes were hauled off the streets.
Ho Chi Minh City, formerly known as Saigon, won a reputation as a den of pimps and prostitutes during the Vietnam War which ended in 1975 and has never shaken off its freewheeling image.

Vietnam's Communist leadership, anxious to maintain its grip on the country, has reacted with alarm to some of the social changes brought about by a decade of reform and open-door policies and has vowed to fend off threats to traditional culture.
